stem: Ten indivisible objects have weights 8, 8, 6, 6, 4, 4, 3, 3, 3, 3. Each bin can hold total weight at most 10. Objects cannot be split. What is the minimum number of bins?

author_certificate.lower_bound: The two 8s require separate bins and cannot share any remaining object. Remaining weight is 32, requiring at least four more bins.

stem: Seven symbols occur 3, 5, 8, 12, 17, 24, and 31 times. Assign each symbol a distinct binary codeword so that no codeword is a prefix of another. There is no alphabetical-order constraint. What is the minimum total number of bits for encoding all 100 symbol occurrences?
What is the determinant of the 4 by 4 matrix with rows (3, -1, 2, -2), (1, 2, 2, -2), (1, -1, 7, -2), and (1, -1, 2, 5)?

Eight workers A through H can each perform at most one task, and each task can be assigned to at most one worker. Eligible task sets are A:{1,2}, B:{2,3}, C:{1,3}, D:{1,2,3}, E:{4,5}, F:{5,6}, G:{6,7,8}, H:{4,7,8}. Assigning every worker is optional. What is the maximum number of tasks that can be assigned?

author_certificate.upper_bound: A,B,C,D can occupy only three tasks.

stem: A fair coin is flipped independently until the consecutive four-flip pattern HHTH first appears. Counting all flips from the start, including the final four, what is the expected number of flips? Overlapping candidate occurrences are allowed.

A single machine can run any subset of these jobs. Each tuple is (start time, end time, profit): [(0, 3, 12), (1, 2, 5), (2, 5, 15), (3, 4, 6), (4, 7, 18), (5, 6, 7), (6, 9, 21), (7, 8, 8), (8, 11, 24), (9, 10, 9), (10, 13, 27), (11, 12, 10)]. A job occupies the half-open interval [start,end); jobs ending exactly when another begins are compatible. No job may be split, shifted or repeated. What is the largest achievable total profit?
